input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 gives only cause-based, insolvency and Customer-specific triggers (9.1–9.3), and Section 27.3 a force-majeure exit; there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and Section 2.1 expressly denies termination rights across a three-year committed term (Section 8.1). That is walk-away territory under T4C (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term), so it fails the fallback. Vendor has no convenience right, which is favourable to us; we make that explicit rather than leaving it to inference. Section 10.2 already requires refund of prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, so no new refund mechanic is needed. We therefore add a 30-day Customer convenience right at the preferred level and conform Section 2.1, preserving its no-reduction restriction.

proposal.summary: Add Customer 30-day convenience termination right and bar Vendor convenience termination; conform take-or-pay clause
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a convenience exit: we have added a Customer right to terminate on thirty days' written notice (with the existing Section 10.2 pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees applying) and confirmed Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term. We also conformed the take-or-pay sentence in Section 2.1, which otherwise denies us any termination right, while leaving the no-reduction restriction intact.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
